column1: Valuation of insurance contract liabilities (being insurance and reinsurance contract assets and liabilities) in the consolidated financial statements
See notes 2(c), 2(z), 4, 5, 6, 23 and 34 (g) to the consolidated financial statements

column2: How the matter was addressed in our audit

column1:
At 31 December 2024, the Group held insurance contract liabilities as well as
reinsurance contract assets and liabilities as a result of its insurance operations. The
Group applies IFRS 17 Insurance contracts to insurance contracts and reinsurance
contracts it holds.
In valuing insurance contract liability and asset balances, management applies
significant judgment. Various assumptions are made including probability-weighted
estimate assumptions regarding the expected claims and lapses, expected premiums
on insurance contracts, expected directly attributable expenses, commission and
charges. Changes to these assumptions may result in material changes to the
valuation.
column2:

Using our actuarial expertise, we assessed the valuation methodology and
assumptions for compliance against the latest actuarial guidance, legislation and
Group accounting policy in accordance with IFRS 17.
